name: Employer ignoring written salary requests
expected: Recommends issuing formal legal demand notice granting 15 days before approaching Labour Authority.
prompt: I sent three reminder emails for my salary to HR and management. They have not responded for 3 weeks.
raw_response:
Hello! I understand how stressful it is to face delayed salary payments and silence from HR, but I am here to help you navigate this legally.

### | Your Situation
You are an employee who has sent three reminder emails to your HR and management regarding unpaid salary, but you have received no response for three weeks. Your primary issue is securing your delayed earned wages and compelling a formal response from your employer.

### | Your Legal Position
- Under Section 5 of The Payment of Wages Act, 1936, wages must be paid before the expiry of the 7th day after the last day of the wage period (or 10th day if more than 1,000 persons are employed), making extended delays unlawful.
- Under Section 7 of The Payment of Wages Act, 1936, any arbitrary or unauthorized withholding of your salary constitutes an illegal deduction, as deductions can only be made for strictly permitted statutory reasons.
- Under the applicable State Shops and Commercial Establishments Act governing your place of work, commercial employers are legally required to clear all earned salary and final dues within the prescribed statutory timeframe upon demand or termination.
- Under Section 73 of The Indian Contract Act, 1872, you are entitled to claim compensation for financial loss or damage caused to you due to the employer's breach of the employment contract regarding timely salary payments.

### | Practical Next Steps
1. Gather evidence, including your employment contract, offer letter, payslips for previous months, bank statements showing the payment history, and copies of the reminder emails sent to HR.
2. Send a formal written demand notice to your employer and HR granting 15 days to clear all outstanding salary dues in full.
3. Approach the appropriate forum, such as the designated Labour Commissioner or the Authority under the Payment of Wages Act, to file an official claim for delayed wages with compensation.

### ℹ️ Information I still need from you
Could you please tell me your state or city of employment, and the exact total amount of unpaid salary currently due?

citations.title: Time of payment of wages and Claims arising out of deductions from wages or delay in payment
citations.description: Wages must be paid before the expiry of the 7th day after the wage period (or 10th day if more than 1,000 persons employed). Section 15 provides for application to the designated Authority for delayed wages with compensation up to ten times the amount deducted/delayed.

citations.act_name: State Shops and Commercial Establishments Acts
citations.section: Settlement of Dues and Service Conditions Provision
citations.title: Statutory Payment of Earned Salary and Notice Pay for Private/Commercial Employees
citations.description: State-specific legislation (e.g., Delhi Shops Act, Karnataka Shops & Commercial Establishments Act, Maharashtra Shops Act) governing commercial and IT/office establishments. Mandates clearance of earned wages and final settlement upon termination or resignation within 3 to 15 days.

citations.title: Compensation for loss or damage caused by breach of contract
citations.description: When a contract has been broken, the party who suffers by such breach is entitled to receive, from the party who has broken the contract, compensation for any loss or damage caused to him thereby.

citations.title: Deductions which may be made from wages
citations.description: Strictly enumerates permissible deductions (such as authorized provident fund, income tax, or willful damage shown after formal inquiry). Any arbitrary or unauthorized deduction is unlawful.
